summary.text: 星 means “star.” Its traditional analysis combines 晶, a pictorial group of stars that contributes the meaning, with 生 as a phonetic element; accounts differ on when 生 entered the written form.

formation.text: The traditional analysis is phonosemantic: 晶 depicts a group of stars and contributes the star meaning, while 生 is identified as the sound element. Early graphic accounts differ: some describe star imagery with 生 already present in oracle forms; others propose a 晶-based spelling before 生 was added.

components.text: 晶 is analyzed as a group of stars, supplying the pictorial image and star meaning. Accounts differ on whether a 晶-based spelling preceded forms that included 生.

生 is identified as the phonetic element. Modern Mandarin and supplied historical readings allow comparison with 星, though those comparisons alone do not establish the role. Accounts also differ on when 生 appeared in the graph.

sound_limitation.text: The character analysis identifies 生 as phonetic, but the supplied reading comparisons do not independently prove its historical role; the cited character-specific 生 reconstruction was not externally verified in this research.

sound.text: The present-day readings provide a modern comparison; they do not establish the ancient sound relation.
In the supplied Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese data, the readings share medial and final material but differ in their initials; this is a comparison, not proof of the graphic role.
The supplied Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms share the final sequence but differ in initial structure; the 生 row was not externally verified in this research.

history.text: The curated oracle-style form is a modern digital redraw. Accounts differ on whether early forms already paired star imagery with 生 or whether a 晶-based spelling came first; the sequence is unsettled, and the accounts do not establish corruption.
Later forms are described as reducing the star depiction 晶 to 日 while retaining 生, though the accounts do not resolve every stage of this graphic development.
A historical dictionary describes 星 as a shortened form of 曐.

uncertainties.text: The early graphic accounts may describe different forms or competing analyses; they do not settle when 生 entered the graph.
The sound comparisons are documented, but the supplied 生 reconstruction was not externally verified here, and sound similarity alone does not prove the historical phonetic role.

senses.period: dating unresolved; oracle-bone-period forms are reported
senses.text: The character analyses identify “star” as the original sense. Reported early forms do not establish a precise first occurrence.
A Western Zhou bronze inscription uses 星 in a personal name; this does not establish the first use of 星 for “star.”

senses.period: oracle-bone period; dating and reading disputed
senses.text: An oracle-bone example is interpreted as 星 used for 晴, “clear weather.” A Shijing phrase is also read this way, but that interpretation is disputed; neither establishes a secure first occurrence or a semantic path from “star.”
Later scattered and numerous uses are recorded, but their first occurrences and development from the star sense are not established.

senses.period: Warring States/Qin slips and Han silk manuscripts
senses.text: In these manuscripts, 星 is reported as a borrowed graph for 腥. The written sign was reused for a different word; this is not a development of “star” into “fishy.” The old object-name and sound match are not established here.

developments.text: An early example is interpreted as 星 for 晴, and a link to visible stars is proposed, but both the reading and the semantic relationship remain uncertain.
Scattered and numerous meanings are recorded, but no intermediate steps from the star sense are established.

Later manuscripts reportedly reuse 星 to write 腥. This is borrowing the graph for a different word, not a change in the meaning “star”; the available evidence does not provide an independently established ancient sound comparison.

limitations.text: The examples record a star sense, a Western Zhou personal-name use, a disputed clear-weather reading, later scattered or numerous uses, and graph borrowing for 腥. They do not establish a complete chronology or the links among all these uses.

items.period: Shang oracle-script style; modern digital redraw based on catalogued form HB2813
items.caption: This oracle-style 星 form has a tall central stroke with short branches and several surrounding enclosed marks. It is presented as a modern redraw of a catalogued Shang-style form; interpretations of how the star-like element and 生 relate in the earliest forms differ.
items.alt: Black oracle-style glyph with a tall branched central shape and four separate enclosed marks around it.
items.selection_reason: The visible form is legible and relevant to 星’s early graphic history. It helps show the form discussed in accounts that connect 星 with a star depiction and 生, while leaving the disputed early sequence open.
